thread.title: European markets bounce day after Apple-triggered turmoil

author: Emily Horton
title: European markets bounce day after Apple-triggered turmoil
text:
European markets bounced back on Friday, a day after Apple’s sales projection downgrade triggered a global downward spiral for markets.
Oil stocks gained, while media and manufacturing stocks were under pressure.
What did markets do? All European markets were in the green on Friday, with the Stoxx Europe 600 SXXP, +1.52% gaining 1.5% to 339.03, after finishing down 1% on Thursday.
The U.K.’s FTSE 100 UKX, +1.35% jumped 1.4% to 6,785.25 and France’s CAC 40 PX1, +1.37% rose 1.4%%, while Germany’s Dax 30 DAX, +1.83% climbed 1.9% to 10,610.49.
Italy’s FTSE MIB Italy index I945, +2.24% was the biggest regional gainer on Friday, surging 2.1% to 18,610.62.
The euro EURUSD, +0.0790% firmed to $1.1409 from $1.1395 late in New York on Thursday, while the pound GBPUSD, +0.2849% rose to $1.2670 from $1.2634.
What is driving the markets? The likelihood of a global economic slowdown has started to sink into the markets, after Apple Inc. AAPL, -9.96% announced a surprise sales projection downgrade late Wednesday. CEO Tim Cook attributed a sharp fall in iPhone revenue to the reduction in Chinese consumer spending.
However, there was some good news about the Chinese economy on Friday, China’s service sector expanded at a slight quicker rate in December, according to Caixin China services purchasing manager’s index. Trade negotiations between China and the U.S. are also set to resume on Monday, Bloomberg News reported .
In the U.S. on Thursday night, House Democrats passed a spending package in an attempt to reopen the federal government , without funding for President Donald Trump’s U.S./Mexico border wall. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said the “wall is an immorality. It’s not who we are as a nation.”
What stocks are active? Pharamceutical stock Galapagos N.V. GLPG, +5.37% gained more than 5%, as U.S. listed Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.’s BMY, -13.26% $74 billion deal to buy rival Celgene Corp. CELG, +20.69% creates a cancer-drug powerhouse.
Among energy stocks, John Wood Group WG., +4.39% jumped more than 4% and Norway listed oil company Aker BP AKERBP, +5.18% surged 4.8%.
Among decliners, German media company ProSiebenSat.1 Media SE PSM, -5.80% skidded 5.8%. and German manufacturer Osram Licht AG OSR, -4.83% slumped 4.8%.
